exclusions: all rows in the prior 100-row Bioavailability_Ma audit
sampling.allocation_rule: proportional across eligible nonempty Stage-0 primary sources, with at least one row per source
sampling.ordering: source order: hf_bioavailability, fa, fg, fh, oral_exposure; deterministic within-source seeded sample order preserved in /tmp/bio333_sample.jsonl

candidate_rows.support_text: In mice and using a dose of 50 mg/kg, the oral bioavailability of resveratrol when loaded in Eudragit nanoparticles was calculated to be 39%.
candidate_rows.indexed_subject_role: resveratrol is the indexed oral-bioavailability subject; Eudragit nanoparticles are the formulation
candidate_rows.evidence_note: The source explicitly names resveratrol, whereas the stored structure is trimethoxystilbene. PubChem CID 445154 supplies the trans-resveratrol identity used as the replacement.

candidate_rows.support_text: Apigenin-loaded W/O/W emulsions prepared by multilayer emulsion showed an oral bioavailability improvement of 4 times (AUC values).
candidate_rows.indexed_subject_role: apigenin is the indexed active; the W/O/W emulsion is its formulation
candidate_rows.evidence_note: The source explicitly names apigenin, but the stored value contains apigenin plus an unrelated sorbitol component. PubChem CID 5280443 supplies the single-compound apigenin replacement.

candidate_rows.support_text: GSK2636771 is an orally bioavailable inhibitor that induces apoptosis in p110β expressing cells; in patients with advanced solid tumors, a dose of 400 mg/day was influential.
candidate_rows.indexed_subject_role: GSK2636771 is the indexed orally bioavailable inhibitor
candidate_rows.evidence_note: The stored structure resolves to capivasertib rather than GSK2636771. PubChem CID 56949517 supplies GSK2636771.

candidate_rows.support_text: The oral bioavailability of cryptotanshinone in rats was reported as 2.05%.
candidate_rows.indexed_subject_role: cryptotanshinone is the indexed oral-bioavailability subject
candidate_rows.evidence_note: The source names cryptotanshinone, while the stored structure is danshensu. PubChem CID 160254 supplies cryptotanshinone.

candidate_rows.support_text: Phase 1 evaluation in patients with relapsed or refractory lymphoma showed that CPI-0610 demonstrated good oral bioavailability and stability (t1/2 = 23 h).
candidate_rows.indexed_subject_role: CPI-0610 is the indexed orally bioavailable investigational drug
candidate_rows.evidence_note: The source names CPI-0610, but the stored structure is an unrelated compound. PubChem CID 57389999 identifies CPI-0610 (pelabresib).

candidate_rows.support_text: Following oral administration of MeIQx, the amounts of labelled material excreted in urine and faeces are very similar to those following i.v. or i.p. dosing, suggesting that oral MeIQx is extensively bio-available.
candidate_rows.indexed_subject_role: MeIQx is the indexed orally administered heterocyclic amine
candidate_rows.evidence_note: The stored structure resolves to MeIQ, not MeIQx. PubChem CID 62275 supplies MeIQx.

candidate_rows.support_text: The pellet formulation released 88.76 % of fexofenadine in phosphate buffer pH 7.4 within 30 min.
candidate_rows.indexed_subject_role: fexofenadine is the indexed released drug; the pellet is the formulation
candidate_rows.evidence_note: The support text names fexofenadine, but the stored structure is febuxostat. PubChem CID 3348 supplies fexofenadine.

candidate_rows.support_text: Based on mass‑balance, the human permeability of amoxicillin for the 250 mg dose was reported as 1.23 × 10⁻⁴ cm/s and classified as high.
candidate_rows.indexed_subject_role: amoxicillin is the indexed permeability subject
candidate_rows.evidence_note: The support text names amoxicillin, while the stored structure is clavulanic acid. PubChem CID 33613 supplies amoxicillin.

candidate_rows.support_text: Table 2 lists the hepatic first‑pass bioavailability (Fh) for S‑VP as 0.130.
candidate_rows.indexed_subject_role: S-VP is the indexed enantiomer for the hepatic first-pass measurement
candidate_rows.evidence_note: The support text identifies S-VP, whereas the stored value is a small amino-acid/propionate mixture unrelated to verapamil. PubChem CID 92305 supplies (S)-verapamil.

candidate_rows.support_text: Table 2 reports that the hepatic blood clearance of R‑VP was 47.0 ml/min/kg.
candidate_rows.indexed_subject_role: R-VP is the indexed enantiomer for the hepatic-clearance measurement
candidate_rows.evidence_note: The support text identifies R-VP, whereas the stored value is a small amino-acid/propionate mixture unrelated to verapamil. PubChem CID 65808 supplies (R)-verapamil.

candidate_rows.support_text: Recombinant UGT2B7 with 0.5 % crude BSA gave a CLint for AZT of 0.569 µl/min·mg.
candidate_rows.indexed_subject_role: AZT is the indexed UGT2B7 substrate
candidate_rows.evidence_note: The support text names AZT, but the stored fused aromatic heterocycle is unrelated. PubChem CID 35370 supplies zidovudine (AZT).

candidate_rows.support_text: The Cmax for Berberine nanocrystals after oral dosing to rats (n = 6) was 7993.59 ± 1257.51 ng/ml (mean ± SD).
candidate_rows.indexed_subject_role: berberine is the indexed oral-exposure analyte; nanocrystals are the formulation
candidate_rows.evidence_note: The support text names berberine, but the stored structure is baicalein. PubChem CID 2353 supplies berberine.

candidate_rows.support_text: The mean AUC0‑last for emtricitabine (FTC) after the test treatment was 10,700 ng·h/mL with a %CV of 18.1.
candidate_rows.indexed_subject_role: emtricitabine is the indexed test-treatment PK analyte; coadministered antiretrovirals are not the subject of this row
candidate_rows.evidence_note: The support text reports FTC AUC, while the stored value is a four-component antiretroviral mixture. PubChem CID 60877 supplies the single-compound emtricitabine identity.

candidate_rows.support_text: In buffer at pH 7 the half‑life of nobilin was 1.8 h.
candidate_rows.indexed_subject_role: nobilin is the indexed stability subject
candidate_rows.evidence_note: The row lacks SMILES but explicitly names nobilin. PubChem CID 102597438 supplies a defined nobilin structure.

candidate_rows.support_text: Primaquine evaluated in buffer gave 66 % A‑B mass balance, A‑B Papp 29 ± 4.5 × 10⁻⁶ cm/s, 99 % B‑A mass balance, B‑A Papp 34 ± 1.5 × 10⁻⁶ cm/s and an efflux ratio of 1.2.
candidate_rows.indexed_subject_role: primaquine is the indexed bidirectional-permeability subject
candidate_rows.evidence_note: The row lacks SMILES but explicitly names primaquine. PubChem CID 4908 supplies primaquine.

candidate_rows.support_text: The enteric‑coated tablet reached its Tmax at 3.4 h (lag‑time ≈ 2 h) after the 250 mg oral dose.
candidate_rows.indexed_subject_role: the indexed analyte is valproate from the enteric-coated divalproex formulation; adjacent records under the same PMID explicitly identify VPA/divalproex
candidate_rows.evidence_note: This row omits the drug name and SMILES, but its same-PMID record block identifies the 250 mg enteric-coated formulation as divalproex sodium/VPA and later rows store valproic acid. PubChem CID 3121 supplies valproic acid.

candidate_rows.support_text: The rat large intestine effective permeability (Peff) of FD-4 in the control condition was reported as 0.36±0.05 ×10^5 cm/s.
candidate_rows.indexed_subject_role: FD-4 is the indexed intestinal-permeability probe
candidate_rows.evidence_note: The support text identifies FD-4, whereas the stored SMILES is an unrelated defined peptide. FD-4 is a heterogeneous approximately 4 kDa FITC-dextran preparation, so no single exact small-molecule replacement SMILES/InChIKey can be assigned without inventing a structure.

candidate_rows.support_text: With the P‑gp inhibitor CSA, GSKA showed a Papp (A‑B) of 18.6 ×10⁻⁶ cm/s.
candidate_rows.indexed_subject_role: GSKA is the indexed P-gp permeability subject; CSA is the inhibitor condition
candidate_rows.evidence_note: The paper-local code GSKA has no structure in the row and no authoritative exact chemical identity was resolved. A replacement would require guessing.

candidate_rows.support_text: Table 2 lists compound 25 with a Caco-2 permeability of 1.00 ×10⁻⁶ cm/s.
candidate_rows.indexed_subject_role: compound 25 is the indexed Caco-2 permeability subject
candidate_rows.evidence_note: The row provides only a paper-local compound number and no structure. No authoritative exact identity was resolved from the available provenance.

candidate_rows.indexed_subject_role: MTB4 is the indexed solubility subject
candidate_rows.evidence_note: MTB4 is a paper-local formulation or solid-form code without a resolvable exact parent structure in the row. No trustworthy single replacement was identified.

candidate_rows.indexed_subject_role: L 14085 is the indexed intestinal-absorption subject
candidate_rows.evidence_note: The legacy code L 14085 is not accompanied by a structure, and no authoritative exact identity was resolved from the available provenance.

candidate_rows.evidence_note: The row provides only a paper-local compound number and no structure. No authoritative exact identity was resolved from the available provenance.
